item.title: Alcohol may weaken cancer immunotherapy, early research suggests
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Useful information on the interaction between alcohol and cancer immunotherapy with clear detail.

Alcohol may weaken cancer immunotherapy, early research suggests

Cancer immunotherapy has transformed treatment for several advanced cancers, yet the difference between these treatments working and not could depend on simple routine habits. A recent study published in Science Signaling explores one such overlooked factor: regular alcohol consumption.

The focus was on immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), a class of drugs that includes anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) therapies that train the body's immune system to attack tumor cells. The researchers used a mouse model and human clinical data to investigate how regular alcohol consumption impacts the success of ICIs.

The effects were evident in both animal models and human patients. In mice with lung and bladder cancer, moderate-to-heavy alcohol consumption cut the success of immunotherapy by nearly half and increased the likelihood of tumors returning. A similar pattern emerged in human clinical data, where lung cancer patients who regularly consumed alcohol, more than one drink a week, experienced fewer survival benefits after starting anti-PD-1 treatment.

Alcohol breaks the brakes

The body's immune system relies on specialized white blood cells called T cells to seek out and destroy cancer cells. To prevent these immune cells from becoming overactive and attacking healthy tissues, T cells have natural off-switches, including a receptor protein called programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1).

Cancer cells can hijack this mechanism by activating the PD-1 off-switch on T cells, effectively putting the brakes on the immune system and allowing tumors to escape attack. Anti-PD-1 drugs, such as pembrolizumab and nivolumab, use engineered antibodies that bind to the PD-1 receptor and block it. This releases the brakes on T cells, allowing them to recognize and attack cancer cells. While these medications have been found to be quite effective in clinical practice, some patients do not benefit from them as much as expected.

Alcohol could be one reason why. Previous studies have found that it interferes with the immune system's response against the tumor. Doctors thus actively advise cancer patients to avoid alcohol. Yet, alcohol consumption remains common among people with cancer, with one study finding that 76.4% continued to drink.

To understand how alcohol interferes with immunotherapy, the researchers turned to mice with lung and bladder cancer. For five weeks before introducing cancer cells, they gave the animals moderate or heavy amounts of alcohol to mimic human drinking habits. They then treated the mice with immunotherapy and tracked tumor growth, survival and recurrence. The researchers also examined electronic health records of cancer patients who had received anti-PD-1 treatment at the UNC Chapel Hill Cancer Hospital between 2014 and 2018.

Weakening the effect of ICI therapies

The study discovered that regular alcohol consumption significantly weakens cancer immunotherapy, but there is a way to restore its effectiveness. Moderate-to-heavy alcohol consumption reduced the success of ICI therapies by about 50% in mice, and in human patients, too, drinking more than one drink per week was associated with reduced survival benefits.

They found that alcohol exposure reduced the overall number of tumor-killing T cells (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells) entering the tumor microenvironment. It also impaired CD8+ T cell activation, reducing their ability to produce key tumor-fighting signals like interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and kill cancer cells. Alcohol also causes T cells to express higher levels of a second inhibitory receptor called TIGIT, whose original job is to prevent immune cells from becoming overactive and attacking healthy tissues.

Antidote to alcohol's effect

To counter this effect, researchers combined standard anti-PD-1 therapy with an anti-TIGIT antibody. Blocking both PD-1 and TIGIT simultaneously prevented these two mechanisms from holding back the immune response. In alcohol-exposed mice, the combination restored complete tumor response rates to almost the same level as in mice that had not consumed alcohol.

The findings together identified the mechanism by which regular alcohol use can impair the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors, like anti-PD-1 therapy against cancer. Future studies will need to use precise alcohol intake numbers to better understand how drinking affects ICIs. For that to happen, the researchers suggest that adding patients' alcohol use to cancer databases would not only help show how it affects different treatments across cancers but also help identify potential solutions.

TIGIT Gene

item.title: Independent review ordered into surgery carried out by NHS Grampian
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Significant issue in healthcare with clear reporting and context.

Independent review ordered into surgery carried out by NHS Grampian

The Scottish government has ordered a review into hepatobiliary surgery at NHS Grampian after a whistleblower leaked a document showing 19 avoidable deaths at the health board.

Dr Mohammed Habib claimed he had contacted the Scottish government on four separate occasions and had gone to the police and the lord advocate with his concerns about patient safety at the board.

In a report from 2022, which was only released by Habib on Thursday, it was found 19 of the 31 deaths in liver and pancreatic surgery cases were avoidable.

NHS Grampian chief executive, Laura Skaife-Knight, said the board would be "open and transparent" in co-operating with the review.

Habib also said two people had died after having the wrong procedure performed on them and has called for the health board to face a corporate homicide inquiry.

Health Secretary Angela Constance said the review would assess how concerns raised about liver, gallbladder and bile duct surgery, including those by Habib, were handled by the board and the Scottish government.

She said it would identify weaknesses in governance, missed opportunities, unreasonable delay, and gaps in accountability.

Constance said Habib's concerns were "deeply concerning and of the utmost seriousness".

"Following discussion with the first minister, I am today commissioning an urgent and fully independent review of how concerns about hepatobiliary (HPB) surgery in NHS Grampian was handled, including the 2022 report into the deaths of patients who underwent HPB surgery," she said.

"Patient safety and high-quality care must always be the first concern of all those who work in, and with, the NHS."

She said that if any patients had questions or needed advice and support they should contact the NHS Grampian helpline on 08085 202030.

One patient told BBC Scotland News he "technically died" after undergoing liver surgery at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary.

Derek Appleton said he believed mistakes had been made during a procedure to remove 60% of his liver after being diagnosed with stage four cancer.

He said he lost 11 litres of blood and went into cardiac arrest, but was never given a proper explanation for what happened.

Constance will make a statement in Holyrood on Tuesday, where she is expected to lay out the timetable and announce who will lead the review.

She said: "My thoughts are with anyone who has lost a loved one and I am acutely aware of the courage it has taken Dr Habib to come forward.

"I recognise he has sought to do this repeatedly, over a number of years, to both to the Scottish government and several other bodies.

"Patients and staff in Grampian have the right to expect full transparency and independent assurance that when valid concerns are raised, they are properly and robustly pursued. That is what this review will seek to establish."

Skaife-Knight said the review was the "best way forward".

She added: "We know the allegations which have been the subject of significant media interest in recent days will cause further concern for patients and families, our communities and staff.

"We will take immediate steps to secure and preserve relevant information, files and records as part of this process."

'Dramatic action'

Humza Yousaf was health secretary at the time of Dr Habib's report.

He told BBC Scotland News he supported "further dramatic action" being taken in relation to NHS Grampian.

A spokesperson for Yousaf - who went on to become first minister before resigning in May 2024 â said: "Humza supports full transparency about what happened at NHS Grampian and will co-operate fully with any review that takes place.

"He has made it clear that he supports minutes from the period in question being released.

"As health secretary, Humza met whistleblowing champions in health boards across Scotland, and he remains clear that staff who raise patient safety concerns must be listened to and protected.

"It takes real courage to do what Dr Habib has done, and he should be commended for refusing to let these concerns go."

The Scottish government has said action will be taken quickly when required as part of the process to refer any issues â including potential criminality â to the relevant authorities without waiting for the final report.

The announcement comes after First Minister John Swinney announced a review of how the government handles correspondence, after he claimed he first heard of three letters sent to him by Habib on Thursday.

On Tuesday, Constance appointed an expert health team to oversee NHS Grampian improvements.

She said the "external intervention support team", comprising experienced senior NHS leaders, would work alongside Grampian's health team to provide "intensive turnaround support".

Healthcare Improvement Scotland has also been asked to complete an early review of NHS Grampian within three months to assess progress, followed by ongoing reviews, to provide independent assurance.

'Excruciating' wait for answers

Scottish Labour's health spokeswoman, Jackie Baillie, said the review was "welcome", adding that a similar situation "must never happen ever again".

She said: "Were it not for the bravery of Dr Habib in this week speaking out, we may never have known just how far this went.

"Grieving families who lost loved ones in the care of NHS Grampian deserve the full truth of what happened at the health board, including who knew what was going on, when they knew, and why it has taken this long for these concerns to come to light."

Yi-pei Chou Turvey, Scottish Liberal Democrat MSP for north east Scotland, said the wait for answers for the families of affected patients had been "excruciating".

She added: "SNP ministers ought to have been battering down the door of NHS Grampian after receiving multiple warnings from Dr Habib and a report uncovering 19 avoidable deaths.…

item.title: 'It gives me the ick': Can you cheat on someone with a video game?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Interesting topic but less relevant to the reader's interests and more focused on entertainment.

'It gives me the ick': Can you cheat on someone with a video game?

Imagine your partner spending hours flirting with someone else, trying to hold their hand and taking them on dates. Most people would have questions.

But what if that someone only exists inside a video game?

The latest instalment in Rockstar's blockbuster Grand Theft Auto franchise has already set sales records, making $3.8bn (Â£2.9bn) in its first day alone.

At the heart of the game is the relationship between its two main characters, Jason and Lucia.

Rockstar says the Bonnie and Clyde-style duo do not have to maintain a full romantic relationship to progress the game.

But their connection can grow by spending time together outside of the main crime and life-on-the-run storyline â through shopping, visiting bars and restaurants and working out together.

Smaller interactions like holding hands and quickly responding to each other's texts can help build a bond.

The idea has restarted a debate almost as old as gaming itself: if you are that invested in a fictional relationship, is your real-life partner entitled to be upset?

In September, polling company YouGov put that question to more than 4,000 British adults.

About 6% said they would regard it as cheating, while a further 19% said they would "not be okay with it". Women were considerably more likely than men to take a dim view.

Alli Franco, a 30-year-old Texan who posts anime and gaming content to more than a million followers, external on TikTok, says she felt "dismayed" watching the debate unfold online.

"If your partner is insecure about a fictional character, then there needs to be some serious reflection," she told the BBC.

"It's similar to having a crush on a TV star, but even further removed from cheating since there is no other actual person involved.â

After Franco posted a video on the subject, hundreds of commenters appeared to agree with her, although some did have reservations.

"To be honest, it depends," wrote one. "If you're cancelling plans with your significant other or directing your intimacy towards a fictional character, then that is a little odd."

"It's very odd and it really gives me the ick," another woman told us.

Mimicking social relationships

For decades, video games have allowed players to build relationships with non-player characters, or NPCs.

Gamers could marry villagers in Harvest Moon in 1996, shape emotional storylines in Final Fantasy VII and pursue more complex romances in role-playing games like Baldur's Gate II.

In life simulator The Sims, they could flirt, date, marry and have children with computer-controlled characters.

But all those interactions were tightly scripted, based on rules and storylines written in advance by game developers.

GTA 6 offers something more dynamic, allowing players to shape the relationship between Jason and Lucia through a wider range of open-world interactions and choices.

"The more sophisticated games get, the less likely it is that players get pulled out of the experience," says Arienne Ferchaud, an associate professor at Florida State University who studies how people form connections with fictional characters.

"Games are doing a better job of mimicking reality and mimicking social relationships."

Grand Theft Auto 6 may represent the current cutting edge of game design, but the next leap forward could come from artificial intelligence.

Nvidia, Ubisoft and other huge tech companies are already experimenting with generative AI systems that allow players to hold more natural conversations with NPCs.

Future characters could remember past encounters, react to a player's actions and build relationships that change over time rather than following a pre-written script.

Ferchaud believes that could make games feel even more immersive.

"You could have relationships that feel more solid or more special," she says, although she argues AI as it exists today would still be creating "a stronger illusion" rather than a genuinely meaningful connection.

Whether that is exciting or unsettling may depend on the player, and there has been some resistance to the wider use of the technology in gaming.

Franco says she is already seeing adverts for AI chatbots that let fans talk to their favourite anime characters.

"I can definitely see AI integrating into games and making it a more realistic experience," she says.

"But should that happen I would still see it as just a game. At the end of the day you can't cheat with lines of code."

item.title: Cigarettes on silver platters at Bondi ‘clean’ beauty business lip gloss launch referred for investigation
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Promotional content with potential health risks, not suitable for the reader's interests.

An Australian beauty company that promotes “clean” ingredients “free from skin irritants” has been referred to state health regulators after appearing to offer cigarettes to guests at a beachside lip gloss launch.

“Celebrating the launch of our soft gloss with our community,” one post from the event shared by the Copini Beauty account on Instagram read, with an accompanying carousel of images showing what appeared to be cigarettes on display with Copini-branded match boxes, lipglosses and glasses of wine.

The images are also featured in a highlight reel from the event on the official Instagram page for the brand.

Copini is co-founded by influencer Casey James and product developer Carla McGraw.

Under the Public Health (Tobacco and Other Products) Act 2023, advertising or promoting smoking or the use of tobacco products is prohibited. Both state and federal laws prohibit businesses offering, giving or distributing a free tobacco product.

Any tobacco supplied must also meet strict product standards, such as displaying mandatory graphic health warnings. The cigarettes at the Copini launch do not appear to carry any health warnings on the filter as required, indicating they are illicit products. Buying or supplying illicit tobacco is illegal in Australia, regardless of the quantity.

Cigarettes in Australia cannot legally carry brand logos. The cigarettes appear to carry the Manchester “sapphire blue” branding, one of the most common illicit tobacco products in Australia. They are considered unlabelled under Australian law because they do not carry official government health warnings and compliant packaging.

A spokesperson for the NSW health minister, Ryan Park, said of the event and images: “This has been referred to NSW health’s centre for regulation and enforcement.”

The centre works with state and federal authorities to regulate smoking products and has powers to inspect premises, seize illicit stock, issue fines and prosecute offenders.

A spokesperson for the federal health department said the government is “deeply concerned about advertising or promotion that glamorises smoking or the use of tobacco products, or helps normalise tobacco use, particularly where it might reach young people”.

“There is no appropriate place for tobacco products to be used as a promotional prop or to make smoking appear fashionable or appealing,” the spokesperson said.

“The government strengthened Australia’s tobacco laws to reduce the visibility and normalisation of tobacco products and protect Australians from the harms of smoking.”

The spokesperson said allegations of non-compliance with laws are taken seriously, saying the maximum penalty for criminal advertising or sponsorship of tobacco under federal laws is $728,000 for an individual, or $7.2m for a company.

Smoking accelerates ageing and causes more than 16,000 cases of cancer in Australia each year. The display of cigarettes at the launch appears to contradict Copini’s philosophy: “We’re 100% vegan, cruelty-free, and free from skin irritants and endocrine disruptors,” the website says, stating that “clean ingredients” are used in all products.

The company did not respond to requests for comment.

It comes amid growing concerns about the use of cigarettes by brands and in images of celebrities, especially online, with health experts warning it risks normalising and glamorising smoking.

Becky Freeman, a professor of tobacco control with the University of Sydney, said it was “shocking to see the resurgence” of smoking in pop culture and on red carpets.

“But to see this really local example, in Bondi, shows this is not an international phenomena – it’s happening in a country like Australia where we have low smoking rates through strong regulations and health policies,” she said.

item.title: Black Friday deals for liquid Brazilian butt lifts criticised over safety fears
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Promotional content with safety concerns, not suitable for the reader's interests.

Clinics in England are promoting seasonal deals – including for Black Friday – on liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), despite concerns about the risks of the procedure.

The government is consulting on limiting liquid BBLs, vampire facials and deep chemical peels in England to qualified healthcare professionals. The proposals follow the death of Alice Webb, a 33-year-old mother of five, after a botched liquid BBL in a Gloucester salon in 2024. Her family have called for laws against “cosmetic cowboys” to be introduced before more people die.

A liquid BBL involves injecting dermal filler into the buttocks. Plastic surgeons say it can carry significant risks and requires expert skill and training to perform, with large amounts of filler potentially causing serious side effects such as blood clots, fat embolisms and sepsis.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) has already acted against time-limited promotions, concluding that Black Friday offers could rush consumers into deciding on cosmetic surgery without enough time to consider the consequences.

Between April and December 2025, the watchdog found more than 900 ads for liquid BBLs in its advert monitoring system. During that period, only 11.5% of the ads they checked stuck to the ASA’s rules.

It said some ads made claims such as “0% infection rate” or described procedures as “safe”, without properly reflecting the risks involved. Other ads played on body insecurities, promising to “boost your confidence” or “transform your body effortlessly”.

Ashton Collins, the director of Save Face, a government-approved register of accredited non-surgical treatment practitioners, said she was “outraged” by BBLs being advertised as “party-season bargains” with time-limited discounts.

“These are not routine beauty treatments; they are serious medical procedures that can lead to devastating complications,” she said.

“Marketing them this way trivialises the risks, and pressures people to make snap decisions without the time, information or proper consultation they need to make an informed choice.”

She added that Save Face had received 1,004 patient-reported complaints about non-surgical BBLs, hip-dip and breast-augmentation procedures since 2023. More than 50% of the complainants experienced sepsis, 94% required hospital treatment and 43% required surgery.

“The impact on people’s lives can be profound and lasting,” Collins said.

One London provider, Clinic Blvd, recently advertised on social media for a 48-hour deal of 800ml of filler plus 200ml free for £1,300. The post, accompanied by a picture of a woman’s bottom, stated that demand was at “an all time high” and that the deals would not be available to everyone. The clinic also listed breast filler as an option, at £799 for 400ml.

A spokesperson for Clinic Blvd said patient safety and informed consent were its top priorities. “All treatments are subject to individual consultations and clinical suitability assessments,” they said. “We take responsible advertising seriously and remain committed to maintaining appropriate professional standards.”

An Instagram post from De Vere Signature Aesthetics, also based in London, promised 100ml of free filler as a “special limited time offer” added to procedures. Their price for filler falls as the volume rises, from about £5 per ml at the bottom of the scale to about £1.50 at the top, rewarding customers for choosing larger amounts. De Vere Signature Aesthetics was approached for comment.

The Belle Clinic, also in London, advertised a deal online offering 40% off a liquid BBL in autumn to “get ready now for your Christmas party”.

A spokesperson said: “Our current promotion is an autumn and winter seasonal offer … It is not intended to create urgency or pressure anyone into making a decision about an aesthetic procedure. We take the ASA’s guidance seriously and are willing to review our promotional wording to ensure it communicates our approach responsibly.”

Nora Nugent, a consultant plastic surgeon and former president of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS), expressed concern over time-limited discounts. “This is a sales ploy that makes people make quick decisions in case they lose out on the offer,” she said, warning that any special offers, even if not time limited, could encourage people to have treatments they might not otherwise choose.

Gerard Lambe, a consultant plastic and cosmetic surgeon and a spokesperson for BAAPS, said: “People encouraging you to have increased volumes and reduced prices, that’s the worst thing that you could ever do. [You] should never ever do that to people. It increases your risk of complications.”

However, Lambe acknowledged that some private plastic surgeons do offer deals on procedures, saying that the issue of finance is complex, and that lack of affordability could lead people to choose cheaper surgery abroad with a greater risk of complications.

The ASA said its rules made clear that adverts for liquid BBLs must be socially responsible.

“We’ve taken widespread and targeted enforcement action against advertisers breaking the rules, including by trivialising the risks of these procedures, using time-limited promotions to create a sense of urgency and exploiting women’s insecurities,” a spokesperson said.

“We support the introduction of further government measures to regulate the sector.”

Source: The Guardian Health | Published: 2026-11-21 11:08 UTC | Difficulty: 41/100

item.title: PulseFlow: Turning a Webcam into a Real-Time Human-Sensing Experience
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

This is a submission for the Presage SmartSpectra SDK Challenge.

PulseFlow: Turning a Webcam into a Real-Time Human-Sensing Experience

Your body, in real time.

What if exploring your body's physiological signals didn't require a smartwatch, fitness tracker, or specialized hardware?

What if all you needed was a webcam?

That question inspired me to build PulseFlow, a Windows desktop application powered by the Presage SmartSpectra SDK that turns ordinary camera input into a real-time human-sensing experience.

PulseFlow combines contactless heart rate and breathing rate estimation with live charts, guided breathing sessions, and meaningful session summaries.

I wanted to explore how complex physiological sensing technology could become a simple, approachable, and privacy-conscious desktop experience.

What I Built

I built PulseFlow, a desktop application developed with Electron, Node.js, TypeScript, and Presage SmartSpectra.

The application uses a standard webcam to estimate physiological signals and presents them through a minimal interface designed for clarity and ease of use.

Rather than building only a technical monitoring dashboard, I wanted to create an experience that people could interact with.

PulseFlow has three main components:

1. Real-Time Physiological Monitoring

PulseFlow requests two physiological measurements from SmartSpectra:

- Heart Rate: Estimated pulse in beats per minute (BPM).

- Breathing Rate: Estimated respiratory frequency in breaths per minute (br/min).

The application displays accepted readings through live numerical indicators and time-series charts.

Users can also see camera status, signal availability, and feedback when capture conditions need improvement.

2. Guided Breathing

I wanted users to do more than simply observe their measurements.

PulseFlow includes a guided breathing experience with:

- Configurable inhalation and exhalation durations.

- A minimal animated breathing indicator.

- Start, pause, resume, and end controls.

- A synchronized session timer.

- Physiological measurement collection during the exercise.

The breathing animation is driven by the exercise timer, not by artificially generated physiological measurements.

3. Session Summaries

At the end of a session, PulseFlow provides a summary containing:

- Total session duration.

- Average observed heart rate.

- Average observed breathing rate.

- Number of valid samples for each signal.

- Session completion status.

These statistics are calculated from accepted SmartSpectra measurements collected during the exercise.

Design Philosophy

PulseFlow follows a minimalist, monochromatic design direction influenced by modern developer tools and the Geist design language.

The interface emphasizes readable physiological metrics, subtle borders, restrained animations, real-time charts, and contextual notifications.

My goal was to make complex sensing technology feel understandable without overwhelming the user.

Real Measurements, Not Simulations

An important requirement I set for myself was that PulseFlow should not fabricate physiological readings.

During a live test, SmartSpectra successfully provided measurements including:

These values came from an actual demonstration rather than hardcoded data.

When valid measurements are unavailable, the application displays an appropriate waiting state instead of inventing readings.

Demo

I recorded a demonstration showing PulseFlow running with a real webcam and the Presage SmartSpectra SDK.

The video showcases live physiological monitoring, the guided breathing experience, and a completed session summary.

Watch the full demonstration on YouTube

For privacy, the public recording uses anonymized camera imagery while preserving the live physiological measurements displayed by the application.

Code

The complete source code is publicly available on GitHub:

The repository includes the Electron application, native SmartSpectra integration, measurement-processing logic, guided breathing functionality, tests, screenshots, and setup instructions.

Technology Stack

Running PulseFlow Locally

Clone the repository:

git clone https://github.com/Ezequie1Sc/PulseFlow.git

cd PulseFlow

Install dependencies:

npm ci

Create a local environment file.

On Windows PowerShell:

Copy-Item .env.example .env

Configure your Presage SmartSpectra API key in .env:

SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY=your_presage_api_key

Start the desktop application:

npm run dev

A compatible webcam, camera permissions, and a valid API key are required.

The repository's README contains additional information about installation, application architecture, privacy, and troubleshooting.

How It Responds to Human Signals

The Presage SmartSpectra SDK is the foundation of PulseFlow.

The application uses live camera-based physiological estimates rather than simulated datasets.

1. Camera-Based Signal Acquisition

After the user explicitly consents to monitoring, PulseFlow initializes the SmartSpectra Node.js SDK and connects to a selected webcam.

The application requests these metrics:

requestedMetrics: [

MetricType.PULSE_RATE,

MetricType.BREATHING_RATE,

]

SmartSpectra processes the camera input and generates physiological estimates along with signal-validation information.

2. Processing SDK Events

PulseFlow listens for several SmartSpectra events:

Incoming measurement messages are decoded using Protocol Buffers.

The application processes the measurements before forwarding accepted values to the user interface.

3. Validating Physiological Measurements

One of my priorities was avoiding misleading readings.

PulseFlow checks incoming measurements using its validation and filtering logic.

If SmartSpectra cannot provide a suitable signal, the interface communicates that state rather than presenting fabricated numbers.

This makes the experience responsive not only to the physiological readings themselves, but also to whether valid measurements are available.

item.title: Your agent's rule pack is only as good as its install script
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

This is the adapted syndication of a longer review first published on AI Stack Lab: RulePort Review: I Ran Its Installer Six Ways. The blogger version has the full command-by-command transcript.

Your agent's rule pack is only as good as its install script

Every "rule pack" sold to people running two or more coding agents makes the same three promises: one source of truth, one installer, and a drift check that tells you when the files on disk no longer match what you bought. The first promise is an authoring choice. The second and third are code, and code can be tested.

So I tested them. I unzipped RulePort ($1 on Gumroad, 58 files, 12 rules) into an empty directory, copied it to a scratch tree, and ran its installer six ways: dry-run, real, twice to check idempotency, over hand-written files, on a machine with no agents at all, and against deliberate drift. Then I hashed the trees before and after each run so "unchanged" meant a matching sha256, not a hopeful reading of the console.

Four claims held. Two leaked. Here is what that looked like.

The parts that held

The compiler is byte-stable. python3 tools/ruleport.py compile printed compiled 12 rules -> 39 files. I hashed the shipped compiled/ tree, compiled, hashed again, compiled a third time, hashed again. Zero files changed in either direction. This sounds like a low bar and it is not: a compiler that reorders its own output every run makes every commit dirty and turns the drift check into noise. This one is deterministic.

--dry-run actually writes nothing. Not "writes then tells you" — I hashed the target directory before and after and it was empty.

Install is idempotent. First run: 39 files. Second run, same command: every file reported unchanged, and the sha256 map of the whole tree was identical. No duplication, no second marker comment, no churn.

It refuses to eat your own files. I planted a hand-written CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with no RulePort marker and ran the full install. Both were skipped and left byte-identical. --force replaced them deliberately, as documented. That default matters more than the feature list: an installer that silently overwrites a CLAUDE.md you wrote is worse than no installer at all.

The fallback fires. On a fresh HOME with agent binaries stripped out of PATH, install.sh printed no runtimes detected and wrote exactly one file: ./AGENTS.md. The README's claim about the universal fallback is true on a machine with nothing installed.

diff means what an exit code should mean — mostly. Fresh install: in sync — installed files match the compiled pack, exit 0. Append one line to a single .mdc rule and re-run: exit 1, with a real unified diff naming the file. Bad arguments exit 2 with usage. I will take a tool that shouts over one that guesses.

The two leaks

Leak one: diff can report "in sync" over zero files. Run it in a directory where nothing was ever installed and it prints one not installed … — skipped line per runtime, then in sync — installed files match the compiled pack and exit 0. Four runtimes skipped, zero files compared, green tick.

If you follow the README and wire that exit code into CI as your drift gate, a machine where the install never happened passes. You have to read the comparing N file(s) lines, or assert on a file count you expect, instead of trusting the number.

I want to be fair about this: a drift check with nothing to compare arguably is in sync with an empty installed set. But that is not the sentence anyone reads at 2am when the CI is green and the agent is still following last month's rules. A gate that can pass by comparing nothing is exactly the false confidence this class of tool exists to remove.

Leak two: "claude detected" means a claude binary is on PATH. Detection is [ -d "$HOME/.claude" ] || command -v claude. On my box that fired and the installer wrote 14 files into ~/.claude — globally, from a project directory, without asking. The README's table says Claude Code lands in ~/.claude/ (global) or .claude/ (per project), but bash install.sh only ever does the global one. To get a project-local .claude/ you must call python3 tools/ruleport.py install --agent claude --target <dir> directly. I confirmed both by doing both.

Neither leak is dishonest — the behaviour is documented loosely enough to be defensible. But "global by default" plus "green drift check that compared nothing" is a pair of surprises worth knowing before you buy, so they belong in the review, not in a footnote.

What is in the box, counted

- 58 files, 174,768 bytes unpacked, 103,003 bytes as the zip.

- 12 canonical rule files — the only place you edit.

- 39 compiled outputs: 12 Cursor .mdc, 14 Claude Code files (12 skills + CLAUDE.md + a /ruleport-status command), 12 Windsurf, 1 AGENTS.md (24,336 bytes, all 12 rules).

- tools/ruleport.py: 457 lines, imports only argparse, difflib, pathlib, shutil, sys. Standard library, so there is no dependency graph to audit and no network call at compile time.

- install.sh: 111 lines. Plus docs/customization.md and docs/update-policy.md.

The 12 rules are deliberately boring: verify before done, test first, error handling, types and docstrings, security baseline, self code review, database safety, API design, dependency hygiene, git hygiene, frontend accessibility, docs updates. They are the ones that stop the classic agent failure — the confident "done" over untested code, the swallowed exception, the dependency added for a problem the standard library already solved.

Who should skip it

- You run exactly one agent. A compiler that emits four formats is pure overhead for one consumer. Hand-write your rules.

- Your team already maintains a conventions tree that agents read. You have a source of truth; a second one is a liability.

- You need a drift gate you can trust blind. Because of leak one, you must assert on the compared-file count, not the exit code alone.

- You want rules generated from source. This ships opinionated prose, not a linter and not a static analyser.…

Source: Dev.to | Published: 2026-11-22 05:42 UTC

Original link: https://dev.to/the_movie_9b1357e8c99cfaa/your-agents-rule-pack-is-only-as-good-as-its-install-script-3l3o

item.title: Por que o COMP-3 do COBOL ainda derruba integrações com Pix e ISO 20022 (e uma ferramenta open-source)
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Quem trabalha com engenharia de backend em bancos, adquirentes ou fintechs no Brasil conhece bem um contraste curioso: na ponta do cliente, o sistema liquida transações em segundos via Pix e troca mensagens estruturadas em XML/JSON no padrão ISO 20022; no núcleo contábil, porém, uma parcela enorme das instituições ainda processa saldos e lotes em mainframes COBOL.

O ponto de fratura mais silencioso nessa ponte não costuma ser a latência da API, e sim a tradução de dados binários — em especial o formato COMP-3 (Packed Decimal).

O que é o COMP-3 na prática?

Em vez de armazenar dígitos em ASCII/UTF-8 (1 byte por dígito) ou usar ponto flutuante IEEE 754 (que introduz erros de arredondamento inaceitáveis em centavos), o COBOL armazena dois dígitos decimais por byte — um em cada nibble (4 bits) — e reserva o último nibble do último byte para o sinal:

- 0xC: positivo

- 0xD: negativo

- 0xF: sem sinal (unsigned)

Por exemplo, o valor +12345.67 definido como PIC S9(5)V99 COMP-3 ocupa exatamente 4 bytes em disco ou na fila de mensageria: 12 34 56 7C (7 dígitos + 1 nibble de sinal).

Três bugs comuns em integrações Pix / ISO 20022

-

Conversão para float ou double: qualquer passagem intermediária por ponto flutuante binário pode corromper frações de centavo na reconciliação de fim de dia. Use sempre precisão fixa (BigDecimal, Decimal, ou inteiros em centavos).

-

Ponto decimal implícito (V): o V no PIC S9(5)V99 não ocupa espaço em byte. Se o parser errar a escala implícita, R$ 100,00 viram R$ 10.000,00 ou R$ 1,00.

-

Interpretação incorreta do nibble de sinal: tratar 0xD como positivo ou falhar ao ler 0xF gera lançamentos invertidos que só aparecem no batimento contábil.

Ferramenta open-source para depurar direto no navegador

Na Digbijoy Labs construímos um inspetor open-source que roda 100% no navegador (sem backend e sem envio de dados) para codificar, decodificar e visualizar payloads COMP-3 nibble a nibble:

- Inspetor online (zero instalação): https://digbijoylabs.github.io/iron-silicon-bridge/

- Código-fonte no GitHub: https://github.com/digbijoylabs/iron-silicon-bridge

- Referência técnica aberta (CERN Zenodo DOI): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24243905

- Livro técnico (The Iron–Silicon Bridge): https://digbijoylabs.com/books/the-iron-silicon-bridge/

Para quem já trabalhou com modernização de legado ou integração de core bancário com Pix: qual foi o bug mais traiçoeiro de encoding ou paridade de dados que vocês enfrentaram?

item.title: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

- Toyota, Nissan, and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News.

- The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses.

- Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon.

Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.

In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.

The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.

The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.

“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”

item.title: Together.ai: Prompt Leakage for Requests
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

We are notifying customers about a security incident involving a subset of prompts submitted to Together AI’s serverless inference service in June and July 2026. An unauthorized party downloaded stored prompt samples after a credential for a private repository was exposed in a public code repository.

We apologize for this incident. We are reviewing the affected data to determine what information was exposed and which customers require direct notification.

What happened

As part of routine software testing, we collected prompt samples authorized for that use and stored them in a private Hugging Face repository. The samples came from requests to the MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2, and Kimi K2.6 models, primarily on June 24, July 4, July 8, and July 14, 2026.

During development of our public GitHub repository, xorl, an AI coding agent committed a credential that provided access to the private Hugging Face repository. Our automated scanning detected the exposed credential, and we reverted the commit.

During the exposure window, an unauthorized party obtained the credential and used it to download the stored prompt samples. The party subsequently searched those samples for credentials to other services and tested whether those credentials were valid. Five of the credentials tested were canary credentials associated with a Dragos security experiment.

We have no reason to believe the unauthorized party has leaked this data further and understand that it has now been deleted.

Investigation and scope

We have worked with an external forensic investigation firm and law enforcement to investigate the incident.

Based on our review, we have not identified evidence of additional prompt leakage beyond this incident. Our review of the affected prompt contents is ongoing to determine whether sensitive personal information or other customer data was exposed. We will contact affected customers directly as needed with the findings relevant to them.

Changes we have made

Following the incident, we strengthened controls around development workflows, credentials, and customer data. These changes include:

- Using scoped or short-lived credentials, and keyless access where supported, to reduce the potential impact of credential exposure.

- Checking all pull requests for credentials.

- Making zero data retention (ZDR) the default setting for new accounts.

- Updating our development processes governing the use of AI coding agents.

What customers can do

Customers handling sensitive prompt data should enable ZDR in their account settings.

If you have questions about this incident or its potential impact on your organization, contact security@together.ai.

Vipul Ved Prakash

CEO and Co-founder, Together AI

Source: Hacker News | Published: 2026-11-22 03:07 UTC

item.title: Attention Pixel 9 and 10 owners: is it actually worth upgrading to the Pixel 11?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Attention Pixel 9 and 10 owners: is it actually worth upgrading to the Pixel 11?

Pixel 10 owners can skip this one. Pixel 9 owners have a real decision to make.

Google's new Pixel 11 went on sale in August 2026, but new doesn't always mean better. It uses the same 6.3-inch display and 5x telephoto camera as the previous year's model; has the same 12GB of RAM; and its battery is just 15mAh bigger. You'll enjoy double the storage space, but it also costs $899, which is $100 more than the launch price of the Pixel 10.

If the question is whether it's worth upgrading from the 10 to the 11, the answer is no. Keep the phone you've got. If you're a Pixel 9 owner, the advantages are more pronounced. Jumping two generations gets you a telephoto lens, better battery life and an additional two years of software updates, making the upgrade a worthy consideration.

What's new compared to the Pixel 10

With the Pixel 11, you get a Tensor G6 chip, which replaces last year's Tensor G5. Google claims the G6 gives users 25 percent improvements in web browsing speed, alongside 15 percent improvements in app launches. The 48MP main camera gets a larger sensor that's reportedly 56 percent more sensitive to light, and Super Zoom reaches 30x instead of 20x. Wireless charging has increased from 15W to 25W, and the phone now comes with 256GB rather than 128GB.

While 30x zoom sounds impressive, our hands-on testing found that these zoom shots looked fine on the phone's screen but lost a lot of detail once we opened them on a laptop. The phone itself was quick and fluid, though admittedly nothing we threw at it pushed it very hard.

On its comparison page with the Pixel 10, Google lists two camera features as exclusive to the Pixel 11: Magic Capture and Camera Looks. Magic Capture records a short clip and pulls out the best frames as stills, while Camera Looks lets you set and tweak a default filter. However, Android Central's Harish Jonnalagadda argues that most of this year's software additions will reach older Pixels through Google's regular updates anyway. Once you take those away (or, rather, add them to the Pixel 10), you may be essentially paying for a faster chip, double the base memory and quicker wireless charging. That's hard to justify at $899, especially if you bought the Pixel 10 in 2025.

It's a different story for Pixel 9 owners

The Pixel 9 has two rear cameras, a 50MP main and a 48MP ultrawide, and tops out at 8x Super Res Zoom. To that, the Pixel 11 adds a 10.8MP telephoto camera with a 5x optical zoom and optical image stabilization. That's more optical reach than the $799 iPhone 17, which has no telephoto at all, or the $899 Galaxy S26, whose 10MP telephoto stops at 3x. When we reviewed the Pixel 11, that telephoto was its main advantage over phones at the same price. It's not a Pro camera, though. The Pixel 11 Pro's telephoto uses a 48MP, 1/1.95-inch sensor, while the base model makes do with a 1/3.2-inch sensor.

In terms of its battery, the Pixel 9 has a 4,700mAh that Google rates for more than 24 hours, while the Pixel 11's 4,985mAh cell is rated for more than 30 hours. In our testing, the Pixel 11 lasted from 8AM on a Saturday to 7PM on Sunday on a single charge. You'll also get Pixelsnap magnets built in with the 11, so magnetic Qi2 chargers and mounts attach without a case, which can't be done with the Pixel 9. The 11's screen is also brighter, peaking at 3,000 nits against the Pixel 9's 2,700.

Google Pixel software support

Google promises seven years of OS and security updates from the date each Pixel first went on sale in the United States. That puts the end of software updates for the Pixel 9 at August 2031, the Pixel 10 at August 2032 and the Pixel 11 at August 2033, so none of these models are anywhere near being left behind yet. If you're struggling with your Pixel 9's battery life, something which has admittedly led me to prematurely upgrade my phone in the past, a genuine replacement will set you back about $50 at iFixit. Google can also provide price quotes for its mail-in repair service through an online estimator.

In our opinion, Pixel 10 owners should definitely consider hanging on until at least the Pixel 12 because, as we said earlier, you're not getting that much more for your money. The telephoto lens is the real draw for Pixel 9 owners who could benefit from having better zoom — a feature that no software update can add. But if your Pixel 9 still gets you through the day and you rarely venture beyond 2x zoom, there's no pressing reason to fork out $899 right now.

item.title: Samsung vs. LG OLED TVs: What's the difference between them?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Samsung vs. LG OLED TVs: What's the difference between them?

It's not simple to say that one is better than the other.

LG and Samsung continue to dominate the OLED TV market. LG entered the field in 2010 with its humble 15-inch 15EL9500 during the technology's infancy, laying the groundwork for its first 55-inch television in 2012. Throughout the years, LG has slowly built a major foothold in the space with its series of OLED displays. Their crisp colors gives it a unique pop you seldom find in other OLED televisions, even those with more impressive spec sheets.

And you won't find more impressive spec sheets than Samsung OLEDs. Since its return to the OLED TV market in 2022, the company has invested heavily in display-panel innovations to carve out its own niche. Samsung's QD-OLEDs are arguably the sharpest-looking OLEDs you'll find in consumer-grade hardware, outperforming LG's panels in color saturation. Based on that, you might think Samsung would be the clear winner for OLED TVs, yet LG's latest OLED innovations make the decision less black-and-white.

Samsung has continued to struggle to provide accurate information about its televisions, obfuscating which panel technologies it uses. LG has faced similar criticism for its major quality concerns with the launch of the G6. Finding the perfect television goes far beyond finding a good panel type. The brand, the television's software and your viewing area should play a key role in your decision.

Samsung and LG's panel technologies

OLED televisions come in three display panel types: WOLED, QD-OLED, and RGB Tandem OLED. WOLED is the most common display type that LG pioneered and continues to innovate on. These TVs use a white light source that passes through four filters to create color: red, green, blue, and white. The white subpixel layer helps brighten the image after it passes through the filters, but it comes at the cost of text clarity. This is the main technology you'll find in LG televisions and is ideal for high ambient-light environments.

Samsung shook up the OLED space in 2022 with QD-OLED. This technology uses a blue light source that passes through red and green quantum dots. Since the dots convert color rather than filtering it out, these panels tend to have a much wider color gamut and are significantly more energy efficient, which theoretically means they last longer. They're the gold standard for HDR displays, but quantum dot technology makes them ill-suited for bright living spaces; strong light hitting the panel can cause magenta glare.

RGB Tandem OLEDs use multiple emissive layers and a striped subpixel layout to boost brightness, reaching upwards of 1,000 nits per pixel on some television models. That said, the lack of quantum dot technology means RGB Tandems tend to have poorer color accuracy than Samsung's QD-OLEDs. RGB Tandem panels are worth a premium due to the high manufacturing cost.

Viewing experiences and controversies

On paper, Samsung's QD-OLED seems like the best option for most consumers. You can mitigate nearly all of the panel's weaknesses by minimizing light sources in your viewing space, and its color gamut is best-in-class for consumer televisions. However, the biggest deciding factor for OLED television has nothing to do with the television itself: it's the room you'll use it in. The best QD-OLED television will struggle in a room with high ambient light. And while LG does have some form of anti-glare on its OLED displays, it isn't enough to eliminate reflections entirely.

Software is also a major deciding factor. Samsung's amazing color saturation sadly can't be paired with Dolby Vision, as all Samsung OLED television models lack support for it — HDR10 is their substitute. Additionally, LG and Samsung televisions run different operating systems. LG's WebOS is supported for upwards of five years, while Samsung's latest Tizen OS will receive up to seven years of updates.

Brand trust shouldn't be disregarded here. Samsung is notorious for poor quality control across its products, including obscuring panel information in certain models. LG has had a more consistent track record, yet it has faced widespread criticism over privacy concerns. The company's terms of service allowed LG to record user conversations and sell them to advertisers. Consumer backlash led the company to release a statement soon after, though many haven't forgiven LG for the controversy.

item.title: This is what can happen if too many devices are sharing your home network
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

This is what can happen if too many devices are sharing your home network

It doesn’t take much to bring a home network to its knees.

Any home network, regardless of efficiency and performance, can get overburdened when enough devices are connected, each vying for its own slice of the pie. When that happens, it's pretty obvious, with the infamous buffering circle plaguing screens, laggy online gaming, endless download times and the apocalypse landing on your doorstep. It doesn't take much to reach this point either. A single high-end smartphone can eat up quite a bit of bandwidth all by itself.

There are two potential limitations to consider. The first is the internet connection coming into your home via your Internet Service Provider (ISP). The second is the Wi-Fi connection between your router and your devices. A faster internet plan won't fix a weak signal from a router tucked into an out-of-the-way corner. On the flip side, a faster router can't do much with a slow internet service plan.

The knee-jerk reaction is to replace your router, upgrade your internet service plan speed and place the router in a more efficient position. That may indeed help, but not everyone can run out and purchase a Wi-Fi 6 or 7 router and hassle their ISP for faster service and an accordingly higher bill. But you shouldn't have to, as long as you don't mind playing with the numbers.

How many devices can your internet connection handle?

There's no reliable rule that says "100 Mbps internet connection supports a specific number of devices." Instead, estimate how many devices can run simultaneously without bogging everything else down. Netflix, for example, recommends a stable connection of at least 15 Mbps for each 4K stream. Three streams represent about 45 Mbps of recommended capacity without accounting for any overhead throughout the home (even coffee pots connect to Wi-Fi nowadays).

No, this doesn't mean each stream constantly consumes exactly 15 Mbps. We're just using it as a reference number for the purposes of planning things out. If there are 10 devices in the home, each using 10 Mbps, that would equal 100 Mbps. In that case, a 100 Mbps download speed (FCC's minimum broadband requirement) would leave no room to spare if all 10 devices are up and running at the same time. In reality, of course, speeds fluctuate, but it's a helpful little math drill to run if you're trying to stay organized and keep that ridiculous buffering circle off your TV screen.

Upload speeds are important for things like video calls or security cameras uploading footage of squirrels fighting in the front yard. Upload speeds are generally much slower than download speeds, thanks to asymmetrical broadband with ISPs allocating most of the bandwidth to downloads. Once you understand the speeds and the average consumption of a single device, you can plan large downloads or other Wi-Fi-intensive tasks for less busy times.

How many routers do I need in my home?

For the vast majority of households, one router is more than enough. A good mesh system or efficiently placed access points will solve most problems. An additional router makes sense in very specific situations. For instance, if your ISP has no choice but to run your wires and install your gateway in the far corner of your home, running an Ethernet cable from the gateway to a router in the center of your home might work out great.

But your best bet is to start with what you already have, and add to it incrementally on an "as-needed" basis. Switch stationary devices (PCs, consoles, TVs, etc.) to Ethernet, if possible, removing their traffic from Wi-Fi, although their internet activity will still share your broadband connection. A router upgrade is an option if you need something that can efficiently manage more devices. Just remember that advertised device capacity is great, but it can't overcome bandwidth limitations on your ISP plan.

If you opt for a mesh system to complement an ISP gateway, follow the setup instructions closely and don't leave both devices performing routing duties without checking the configuration. If the gateway and mesh remain in their default routing modes, it could create double NAT, which might cause an issue with online gaming or port forwarding. It doesn't need to get too complicated because the end point boils down to addressing what is constraining your system. Crunch the numbers first; decide which direction to go second. You got this!

Source: Engadget | Published: 2026-11-22 00:45 UTC

Original link: https://www.engadget.com/2319295/what-can-happen-too-many-devices-on-home-network/

item.title: Stock market correction? Whatever — Wall Street is bullish on 2027, and one chief investment officer sees the S&P 500 soaring 45% to 10,000
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: provides a comprehensive view of the market's outlook with clear analysis and expert opinions

The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 joined the Nasdaq in correction territory as AI stocks plunged further, but 2026 is also winding down, and Wall Street is already putting out predictions for 2027.

Analysts see solid gains ahead, with the U.S. economy expected to continue chugging along on the back of massive hyperscaler spending and resilient consumers. Some also welcomed the recent decline for taking froth off markets that might otherwise start looking overheated.

Even this week’s selloff, which marked the worst weekly loss since the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic, was largely dismissed as a move driven more by emotion than fundamentals.

“This does not mean stampedes are uninformative or palpitations never presage heart attacks, but today’s panic does not feel like an AI bust,” Viktor Shvets, head of global desk strategy at Macquarie Capital, said in a note Friday.

Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager and partner at Founder ETFs, quipped that the market is “selling first and asking questions later.” And Jamie Cox, managing partner for Harris Financial Group, predicted investors will “return to rationality” and look instead to consumption-boosting GDP.

Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley chief U.S. equity strategist Michael Wilson said earlier this week that the S&P 500 would finish 2027 at 8,700, representing a 26% jump from current levels and a 15% rally when he made the call.

“We see the mid-cycle transition now ending with a more stable mid-cycle backdrop evolving in 2027,” he wrote.

Goldman Sachs also sees the broad market index soaring to 8,700 next year, “albeit with higher volatility than in recent years.”

Peter Oppenheimer, the bank’s chief global equity strategist, said that while corporate earnings growth will slow, inflation, bond yields, and oil prices will also moderate. “We expect the equity bull market to continue.”

Elsewhere, estimates were less bullish but still upbeat. UBS Global Wealth Management put the S&P 500 at 8,200 next year, implying 19% upside from Friday’s close.

Although it sees more earnings gains in 2027, Wall Street is focusing on whether the investment cycle can support profits into 2028, UBS explained.

“Cannibalization, financing, and execution risks around AI have increased while expectations and index concentration remain high,” it added. “The market is therefore more sensitive to earnings disappointment or a further rise in discount rates.”

Wells Fargo’s S&P 500 outlook in 2027 is also for 8,200, which assumes slower profit growth as well.

But then there’s Steve Chiavarone, chief investment officer for equities at Federated Hermes, who has a year-end view of 10,000—or a 45% surge from current levels.

He brushed aside this month’s midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep Congress and several state capitals. While Wall Street fears the blue tsunami will slow the AI infrastructure boom, Chiavarone said risks to the buildout are overblown. Even a slight retreat would be positive.

“A modest pullback in the data center buildout could give cash flows time to catch up, easing inflation pressures and making the investment boom more sustainable,” he argued.

Slower prices could prevent additional rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, which has grown more hawkish as policymakers become impatient with inflation exceeding their 2% target for over five years.

Although Wall Street sees more tightening in the coming months, some analysts also anticipate rate cuts later in 2027 as inflation cools. But that assumes the Iran war will be over some time next year.

For now, Gaurav Mallik, chief investment officer at Modera Wealth Management, described the market slide as a “garden variety correction,” with stock leadership rotating from tech to industrials and financials.

“The pullback in stocks sets the market up nicely for 2027, which we believe will be a high-single-digit year,” he added. “Multiples are shrinking, and total returns are a function of earnings growth, which so far looks robust for 2027.”

Source: Fortune | Published: 2026-11-22 00:02 UTC | Difficulty: 61/100

item.title: The AI bust is a growing threat to China’s economy and a ‘moment of real danger’ for President Xi Jinping, analyst warns
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: addresses a significant economic issue with relevant context and analysis

U.S. investors are facing a meltdown in tech stocks and the possible end of the AI boom, but the bubble has already popped in China, where an even worse market crash threatens the economy and President Xi Jinping, according to Yardeni Research.

China’s tech-heavy STAR 50 index has tumbled 44% from its high this summer, while the Nasdaq is down 18% from its record—even after U.S. stocks suffered their worst week since the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic.

That’s thrown a wrench into Xi’s plans for the economy, Yardeni said in a note earlier this month. While the Chinese leader was riding high as host to global leaders this week, the market’s downturn jeopardizes his plan to turn China’s savers into stock investors who can finance the AI buildout and de-emphasize the property market.

Real estate accounts for roughly 70% of household wealth in China and was traditionally a place to stash savings. But the housing crash has weighed on consumer demand, even producing intermittent deflation. Business investment is also falling, with October data showing property investment sank nearly 22%.

With the domestic market still weak, Beijing has instead relied on a flood of cheap exports to keep the economy growing while also deploying the “national team” of state-backed banks to pump money into the stock market.

But according to Yardeni, Chinese stocks collapsed this year due in part to cutthroat competition, heavier tax burdens, higher energy costs, tariffs, and the risk that China’s trading partners will block exports being sold at ultra-low prices.

“To keep AI funding flowing, Xi needs a buoyant stock market,” the note said. “Otherwise, AI risks being folded into the state-owned enterprise (SOE) universe that his team has pledged to shrink since 2013, further crowding out the private sector.”

Retail investors are also skittish about Chinese stocks after Xi’s government cracked down on the tech sector in 2020. The market’s reputation as a rigged casino that favors politically connected insiders doesn’t help either. In fact, the Shanghai Composite remains well below its October 2007 peak despite China’s GDP exploding nearly sixfold.

Many households now have “financial PTSD” after repeated stock busts, including a crash in the summer of 2015 that required an aggressive national team rescue, Yardeni added.

To be sure, China remains a leader in AI, and mom-and-pop investors still drive most of the trade, even as they treat the market more like high-stakes gambling than a place to grow retirement savings.

“Yet this is a moment of real danger for Xi. A bursting AI bubble would not merely erase wealth or dent China’s technological prestige. It would weaken Beijing’s attempt to replace a broken property model with a stock-market-led one,” Yardeni warned.

“China can build world-class AI models, train engineers, and spend billions on chips. But if its households still view Shanghai as a casino with odds set by the Politburo, Xi’s dream of creating a Chinese version of Wall Street may remain just that: a dream.”

Underscoring its importance to Beijing, Premier Li Qiang told a State Council executive meeting earlier this month that stabilizing capital markets was the top priority for the rest of the year.

It followed securities regulators sharply easing requirements for company buybacks that help lift stock prices and discouraging IPOs and large share sales to prevent stock dilution that triggers selloffs.

But the spy scandal that dethroned Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia represents a new risk to China’s AI ambitions. Backlash over the advanced U.S. chips and computing capacity that China had access to has spurred the Trump administration to impose new technology curbs.

“By targeting both indirect chip shipments to China and its access to overseas computing power, the new controls threaten to slow the catch-up of China’s leading AI models and to slow China’s AI rollout,” analysts at Capital Economics wrote on Tuesday.

Source: Fortune | Published: 2026-11-21 21:45 UTC | Difficulty: 61/100
